headline: AMD Q2 beats but stock -8% AH: rev $11.54B (+50% YoY), Data Center $6.7B (+107%), Q3 guide $13B ± $300M — Helios ships 'this quarter' to Meta/OpenAI/Oracle
summary: AMD reported Q2 AMC Aug 4: revenue $11.54B (+50% YoY, +13% QoQ) vs $11.31B est, GAAP EPS $1.38, non-GAAP EPS $1.66 vs $1.61 est, GAAP gross margin 54% / non-GAAP 56%, non-GAAP op income $3.1B. Data Center revenue $6.7B (+107% YoY, 58% of total) on EPYC + Instinct strength; Client +23%, Gaming -31%. Q3 guide $13B ± $300M (~41% YoY, +13% QoQ) came in ahead of Street's ~$12.8B. Helios rack-scale platform in full production, first shipments this quarter to Meta/OpenAI/Oracle, ramp through Q4 and 1H27. Despite the print, shares fell ~8% AH — the market had been pricing a stronger Helios-driven forecast (Futurum's Newman) and rising capex weighed. CNBC: 'Wall Street analysts say AMD will outperform despite post-earnings slide.'

headline: AMD hyperscaler AI-accelerator commitments quantified on Q2 call: OpenAI 6 GW of Instinct (starting MI450 2H26); Anthropic 2 GW MI450 in Helios (1H27); Meta + Oracle initial Helios customers
summary: Post-print detail on AMD's demand book: OpenAI committed to a multi-year, multi-generation deployment of up to 6 GW of Instinct GPUs, beginning with MI450 in 2H26. Anthropic will deploy up to 2 GW of MI450-series GPUs in Helios racks — first GW starts deployment 1H27, plus a multi-year software collaboration using Claude for ROCm/MI optimization. AMD identified Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle as initial Helios customers, with 'demand for Helios ahead of AMD's initial forecasts.' Read-through: CRWV / Lambda / OCI (ORCL) capex all leaning into MI450 optionality; positive for HBM (MU / 000660.KS / 005930.KS) and Helios rack integrators (SMCI / DELL / HPE / CLS).

headline: Siemens Energy fiscal Q3 record: EPS €1.28 vs €1.16 est (+10%), revenue €11.4B (record), orders €17.9B (record); Gamesa first profitable quarter since Q4 FY22; FY26 outlook 14-16% comp rev growth reaffirmed
summary: ENR.DE beat: fiscal Q3 EPS €1.28 (vs €0.71 YA, €1.16 est) on record €11.4B revenue and record €17.9B orders. Profit before special items more than tripled to €1.6B (14.2% margin); free cash flow pre-tax €2.3B (>5x YoY). Drivers: record Gas Services orders, plus strength in Grid Technologies and Transformation of Industry. Siemens Gamesa turned its first profitable quarter since Q4 FY22 — key milestone in the turnaround. Management reaffirmed FY26 comparable revenue growth of 14-16%. Shares -0.9% at €149.5 on Q4 seasonal softness warning, but the print reinforces the datacenter-power capex thesis. Read-through positive for GEV, ETN, SNEXF.

headline: PLTR retraces 2% overnight after Tuesday's +29.5% blowout pop; UBS lifts PT to $220 from $200, Citi notes results 'weaken bear case around rising AI competition'
summary: After Palantir's +29.5% surge Tuesday (best day since Feb 2024) on the Q2 print, shares dipped ~2% in overnight trading — profit-taking, not a rethink. Analyst desks piled on: UBS raised PT to $220 (from $200), citing 'exceptional growth with revenue acceleration, significant guide increase, and strong US commercial momentum' with 'no signs of competitive pressures.' Citi (Buy $245), Wedbush ($230), D.A. Davidson ($200) all reiterated. DA Davidson's Gil Luria: 'We are running out of superlatives — Palantir is the best technology company.' Citi noted demand for data privacy from AI companies 'sets Palantir apart.'

headline: Middle East tension jolts safe-haven bid pre-open Aug 5: gold +1.83% to $4,228/oz, silver +2.59% to $61.81 on reported Houthi attack on Saudi oil tanker; equity futures still positive
summary: Overnight Houthi strike on a Saudi tanker pushed gold futures +1.83% to $4,228.40/oz and silver +2.59% to $61.81/oz into the Wednesday open. Not enough to derail equity risk-on: S&P futures +0.53%, Dow +0.46%, Nasdaq-100 +0.15%, Russell +0.36% pre-open on Palantir/CAT afterglow and reported Iran-front progress. Watch: any escalation reads into energy costs (indirect drag on hyperscaler power PPAs) and could firm safe-haven metals; near-term neutral for AI infrastructure names but a variable to monitor if Strait-of-Hormuz risk premium builds.

headline: Commerce testimony to Congress (July 14): H200 shipments to China 'very few' despite ~$10B in approved BIS licenses — Chinese hyperscalers accelerating domestic alternatives instead
summary: Commerce Department official told Congress on July 14 that H200 shipments to China have been 'very few' since the January 2026 case-by-case regime opened, even though roughly $10B in export licenses have been approved. Combined with the 25% national-security tariff, 50%-of-US-volume cap, and end-use certification requirements, effective Chinese uptake has been modest. Chinese hyperscalers (Alibaba, Baidu, Huawei/CXMT ecosystem) are accelerating domestic accelerator and HBM development instead — CXMT DRAM share now ~8% in Q1 (from ~3% a year earlier). Net for NVDA/AMD: China revenue capture from the 'thaw' has under-delivered vs bull-case scenarios, but that was already largely embedded in consensus.

headline: Asia risk-on holds pre-Wednesday: memory names extend Tuesday's bounce as AMD Data Center +107% print validates HBM-demand thesis; TSMC read-through to MI450 packaging
summary: Continuation of Tuesday's Korean bounce (Samsung +2.51%, SK hynix +2.94%) as AMD's $6.7B Data Center print (+107% YoY) and $13B Q3 guide validated the AI-accelerator memory-demand thesis. HBM take-away: MI450 shipments 2H26 pull HBM4 supply tighter — SK hynix ~62% HBM market share, Micron entering HBM4 volume for Nvidia Vera Rubin. TSMC read-through positive: CoWoS advanced-packaging demand from MI450 layered on top of Rubin. Samsung 1c DRAM and P5/Pyeongtaek + SK M15X capex plans stay unchanged; the 'supply-constrained through 2028' framing from Amazon holds.
